title: Smallpox Eradication: Vaccination, Surveillance, and Verification
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Smallpox was caused by variola virus and spread only among humans. Its visible illness could be severe, leaving death, scarring, or blindness. Vaccination made prevention possible long before eradication became operationally possible. That delay matters. A scientific tool does not distribute itself, find missed cases, maintain equipment, earn local trust, or adapt a campaign to war, migration, and limited health infrastructure. The history is therefore not a simple line from invention to disappearance.

An intensified global programme began in the late 1960s. Vaccination remained essential, but teams learned that coverage figures alone could conceal transmission. They strengthened surveillance: health workers searched for suspected cases, used recognizable symptoms and identification materials, investigated reports, and mapped chains of contact. When a case was found, isolation and rapid vaccination around the patient could interrupt local spread. This surveillance-and-containment approach concentrated scarce resources where transmission was occurring.

Several biological features made eradication feasible, although none guaranteed success. Humans were the only reservoir, an effective vaccine existed, and the disease usually produced signs that could be recognized. Still, feasibility is not achievement. National programmes, local workers, laboratories, communities, and international institutions had to exchange information and respond across borders. Strategies were revised when local conditions exposed a weakness. The campaign worked not because one plan was perfectly executed everywhere, but because evidence from the field changed practice.

The last known naturally occurring case was identified in Somalia in 1977. That event did not instantly prove global eradication. Special searches continued, and independent review examined whether transmission had truly stopped. In 1980, the World Health Assembly endorsed the conclusion that smallpox had been eradicated. This distinction between a last observed case and a verified absence is central to public reasoning: not seeing a disease is weak evidence unless a system had a real chance to find it. Eradication was thus a combined achievement of vaccination, surveillance, containment, adaptation, cooperation, and certification.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The invention of a vaccine automatically ended smallpox transmission.

options.label: B
options.text: Eradication joined an effective preventive tool to systems that found, contained, and verified cases.

options.label: C
options.text: Finding the last known case was sufficient by itself to prove eradication.

options.label: D
options.text: Favorable biological conditions made cooperation and adaptation unnecessary.

questions.answer: 正解：B。ワクチンは不可欠でしたが、本文は症例探索、封じ込め、現場適応、国際協力、最終確認を結びつけて初めて根絶が達成されたと論じます。A・C・Dはいずれも制度的過程を落としています。

questions.prompt: Why does paragraph 1 distinguish the existence of vaccination from operational eradication?

options.label: A
options.text: Because a scientific tool still had to be produced, delivered fairly and continuously, accepted locally, and linked to systems that verified outcomes

options.label: B
options.text: Because vaccination had no role in preventing smallpox

options.label: C
options.text: Because invention history alone proves that every population received the vaccine

options.label: D
options.text: Because visible symptoms made distribution systems unnecessary

questions.answer: 正解：A。技術の存在と、持続的で公平な配布、信頼、症例発見、成果確認は別です。そのため発明史だけでは根絶までの遅れや実施上の課題を説明できません。

questions.prompt: Which meaning is closest to “conceal” in paragraph 2?

options.label: A
options.text: hide from view or understanding

options.label: B
options.text: measure with complete accuracy

options.label: C
options.text: eliminate permanently

options.label: D
options.text: publish immediately

questions.answer: 正解：A。高い接種率の集計値が局地的な感染継続を「見えなくする」可能性を述べています。conceal は文脈上「隠す」です。

questions.prompt: How did surveillance and containment change the campaign's use of resources?

options.label: A
options.text: They replaced vaccination with laboratory research only.

options.label: B
options.text: They directed case searches, isolation, contact tracing, and rapid surrounding vaccination toward active chains of transmission.

options.label: C
options.text: They treated national coverage averages as proof that no local transmission remained.

options.label: D
options.text: They stopped investigations whenever a suspected case was reported.

questions.answer: 正解：B。平均接種率だけでなく、能動的探索、接触連鎖の把握、隔離、周辺への迅速接種へ資源を集中しました。分析単位を全国平均から局地的感染連鎖へ移した点が重要です。

questions.prompt: Why did favorable biological features make eradication feasible but not guarantee it?

options.label: A
options.text: They removed the need for logistics, trust, reporting, and cross-border coordination.

options.label: B
options.text: They made eradication biologically possible, but institutions still had to locate cases, deliver vaccines, exchange information, and adapt practice.

options.label: C
options.text: They showed that humans were not involved in transmission.

options.label: D
options.text: They prevented workers from recognizing the disease.

questions.answer: 正解：B。ヒトだけが宿主、有効なワクチン、認識しやすい症状は可能性を高めますが、探索、物流、信頼、検査、国境を越える情報交換、適応がなければ成果にはなりません。

questions.prompt: What does paragraph 3 suggest about learning from the field?

options.label: A
options.text: One unchanged plan was executed perfectly in every setting.

options.label: B
options.text: Strategies were modified when local evidence revealed weaknesses in current practice.

options.label: C
options.text: Laboratories completely replaced communities and local workers.

options.label: D
options.text: Scarce resources made targeted containment impossible.

questions.answer: 正解：B。現地条件が弱点を示すたびに戦略を修正したことが成功要因です。中央計画をそのまま反復したのではなく、証拠によるフィードバックが実務を変えました。

questions.prompt: When would the absence of reported smallpox cases become strong evidence of eradication?

options.label: A
options.text: When no one actively searches for cases

options.label: B
options.text: When surveillance is sensitive, broad, and sustained enough that suspected cases are likely to be reported and investigated

options.label: C
options.text: Immediately after the first successful vaccination

options.label: D
options.text: Whenever a country reports high average coverage without checking local transmission

questions.answer: 正解：B。否定的証拠が強いのは、十分な範囲・期間・感度を持つ監視が実際に症例を発見できたはずのときです。探索能力が不明なら「見つからない」は弱い証拠にとどまります。

questions.prompt: What is the function of the sentence “Still, feasibility is not achievement”?

options.label: A
options.text: It denies that biology affected the campaign.

options.label: B
options.text: It contrasts favorable necessary conditions with the social and institutional work required to turn possibility into an outcome.

options.label: C
options.text: It claims that achievement always occurs once a vaccine exists.

options.label: D
options.text: It treats international coordination as a biological property of the virus.

questions.answer: 正解：B。生物学的条件は好都合で必要でも、それだけで達成を生みません。可能性を成果へ変える制度、社会、実務の因果層へ議論を移す接続文です。

questions.prompt: Which revision best corrects the claim that “the vaccine alone eradicated smallpox”?

options.label: A
options.text: The vaccine was indispensable, but eradication also depended on production and delivery, surveillance, isolation, ring vaccination, trust, laboratories, coordination, adaptation, and certification.

options.label: B
options.text: The vaccine was irrelevant because surveillance alone cured infected patients.

options.label: C
options.text: The last case automatically certified eradication without further searches.

options.label: D
options.text: One central organization acted alone and local participation had no effect.

questions.answer: 正解：A。ワクチンを英雄的単独原因にせず、配布、監視、隔離、輪状接種、信頼、検査、協調、適応、1977年後の探索と認証を含む分散した制度として説明します。
